steps.say: A demolition-and-rebuild puzzle. No chemistry yet, just money.

steps.pre: A builder pays £679 to knock down an old shed, then gets £864 back selling salvaged materials while rebuilding. Better off by £

steps.say: That is exactly a bond energy calculation. Breaking bonds is the demolition COST (energy in); making bonds is the salvage PAYBACK (energy out), and ΔH = energy in − energy out. method_card.title: Bond Energy Calculations
method_card.content:
Two halves: bonds broken (energy in) and bonds made (energy out).

For each bond type, multiply its bond energy by the number of that bond, then add within each half. Use the balanced equation's coefficients: 2H2O has 4 O-H bonds, not 2.

ΔH = energy in − energy out. Negative means exothermic; positive means endothermic. Check whether your board gives you the bond energies or expects them stated in the question.

steps: Work the whole reaction: count every bond type on both sides, multiply by bond energies and coefficients, and total each half.
Watch molecules with several bonds: CH4 has 4 C-H, CO2 has 2 C=O, 2NH3 has 6 N-H.
ΔH = total broken − total made. Negative is exothermic, positive is endothermic.

steps: A bond energy sum has two halves: energy to break the reactant bonds (energy in) and energy released making the product bonds (energy out).
For each bond type, multiply its bond energy by how many of that bond there are, then add within each half.
